parsed.explanation: The combined regime's worst documented feature is the national entry and document apparatus, which reaches every outed or document-mismatched trans visitor: sex is defined as birth-assigned, X markers are no longer issued, and the February 2025 cable directs officers to refuse cases where records conflict or sex is doubted, with material-misrepresentation findings supporting lifetime inadmissibility. Unlike the 0.35 anchors, no statute bars detention for marker mismatch, and the detention it can lead into is documented as abusive for trans people. The division adds bathroom bans, a binary-of-sex statute, criminalised minor care, no public-accommodations recourse and a hate-crime law excluding gender identity, atop national counterterrorism language naming pro-transgender groups. Rule-of-law courts here enforce rather than relieve the exposure; mitigants are partial and litigated.

entry_documents.exposure: National order requires birth-assigned sex on documents; X markers no longer issued. Cable instructs refusal where records conflict or sex is doubted, and a material-misrepresentation finding can support permanent, lifetime inadmissibility. Passports reported confiscated or blocked, stranding travellers.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; litigation by a civil-liberties union continues; a legal-aid FAQ on document rules exists.
entry_documents.interaction: A mismatch flagged at a national port of entry escalates within the national system regardless of the division's own rules; fraud finding is discretionary, not automatic.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody documented as abusive for trans detainees: forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement, severe sexual abuse; national corrections policy imposes conversion-style practices and cuts hormones.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Several executive orders blocked or enjoined; corrections bureau policy adopted 2026. No documented custody protocol protecting trans visitors.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document discrepancy at the border can lead to secondary screening, then immigration detention, then placement and treatment by birth sex.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division bans bathroom use by gender identity (2022 schools, 2024 colleges); SB79 declares immutable binary and permits sex-segregated spaces; no statewide public-accommodations protection, so exclusion by venues is lawful.
federal_state_facilities.protection: None statewide; two municipal ordinances and three cities' public-employment protections, which are resident-facing.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National facility restrictions compound the division's bans; a visitor's exposure is mainly permissive exclusion plus the college-campus ban rather than a criminal statute (trespass triggers are documented in other divisions, not clearly this one).

care_services.exposure: Providing puberty blockers, hormones or surgery to anyone under 19 is a Class C felony (10 years) in the division; no insurance-exclusion ban; care records mismatch may surface identity.
care_services.protection: Adult care is not criminalised; national hate-crime statute unrelated. No documented assurance that adult visitor prescriptions or emergency care will be honoured.
care_services.interaction: A traveller with a minor cannot obtain gender-affirming care for them in the division; an adult's refill depends on undocumented facility discretion.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: May 2026 national counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups for rapid neutralisation; a December 2025 justice memo uses 'radical gender ideology'; an order directs investigation and prosecution of school staff supporting trans minors.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Same strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; several orders enjoined in court.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Frames trans advocacy and visible support as security-adjacent, raising official scrutiny of outed travellers who attract attention.

minors_guardians.exposure: A trans minor travelling with a guardian faces unavailable gender-affirming care (provider felony), school-facility bans, and national rhetoric framing their social transition as harm; no statewide accommodations protection.
minors_guardians.protection: No documented penalty, detention or criminal charge attaching to the travelling minor or guardian as such; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian exposure is indirect (care denial, facility exclusion) rather than a documented criminal sanction on the family.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: The division's only violence figure (3.8/100k, described as an undercount floor) carries no usable magnitude; no specific incident is documented. Division hate-crime law excludes gender identity since 1994; no statewide non-discrimination recourse.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National 2009 hate-crime statute covers gender-identity crimes; two municipal ordinances bar discrimination.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: A trans victim in the division relies on national statute and local ordinance; state-level bias-crime coverage is absent.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statewide public-accommodations, housing or employment protection; local remedies limited to two municipalities; hate-crime law excludes gender identity.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National hate-crime statute (2009); federal litigation and injunctions; legal-aid document FAQ. Courts in this circuit have upheld refusal of accurate licences.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists on paper nationally but institutions here enforce the restrictive rules, so it does not offset the exposure.

anchor_checks.comparison: That anchor's worst feature is arbitrary street-level arrest, extortion and humiliation without institutional protection. Here the mechanism is lawful, systematic and documented rather than kleptocratic, but it reaches every document-mismatched traveller and can end in abusive immigration custody and lifetime inadmissibility, so it sits slightly above that anchor.

That anchor expressly bars detention for marker mismatch: the traveller is denied entry and nothing more. Here the analogous mismatch can lead to refusal plus a fraud finding supporting permanent ineligibility, and into custody documented as violent, so this regime is materially below that anchor.

There a statutory guideline and a supervisor ultimately protected the traveller; detention was avoided and a permit issued. Here the national cable points officers toward refusal rather than accommodation, and court rulings in this circuit have upheld the restrictive document practice, so no comparable working remedy exists.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is layered: a national binary-sex document order, an entry cable directing refusal on doubt and contemplating lifetime inadmissibility, and a division that adds bathroom bans, a statutory binary-of-sex declaration, felony criminalisation of minor care, and no public-accommodations recourse. Violence risk is unquantifiable because the sole figure is an undercount floor; state bias-crime coverage excludes gender identity, though a national statute applies. Detention is the sharpest severity: abusive custody for trans detainees is documented, and the entry pathway can reach it. Courts here have enforced rather than relieved the restrictions, so litigation and the national hate-crime statute do not materially offset the exposure.
